triples.rationale: Both Idumea oracles connect the heart's pride or insolence with holes in rocks and an elevated position. Obadiah voices the inhabitant's boast as a question about who can bring him down. Jeremiah announces that the Lord will bring the addressee down despite the elevated eagle's nest.
triples.source_text: The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who camp in holes in the rocks, raising his dwelling high and saying in his heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”

target_units.text: Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.

triples.rationale: Obadiah describes soaring like an eagle and placing a nest among the stars, then announces that the Lord will bring the addressee down from there. Jeremiah likewise joins the elevated eagle's nest with the Lord bringing the addressee down.
triples.source_text: If you soar like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.
